proposedOverrides.summary: The atlas begins Kandy late in 1650 but ends it correctly in 1815, when British invasion and the Kandyan Convention terminated the sovereign kingdom.

fell.text: British forces occupied Kandy and the Kandyan Convention of 2 March 1815 transferred sovereignty to the British Crown.

batchIdentityNotes: Exact target id kandy is indexed as Kandy, circa 1650 to 1815, with no aliases or authored link; the card distinguishes city, capital and sovereign Kingdom of Kandy.

The imported summary's monarchy dates 1469 to 1818 are not adopted. Kandy's secure capital era is treated from the 1590s, sovereign rule ends in 1815, and the 1817 to 1818 uprising is post-annexation resistance.

At 1650 and 1700 the exact shape is one unlabeled 15-position Polygon with bbox 80.03420034200343,6.473453302778211 to 81.39501395013951,8.86864347057223 and SHA-256 8b64cda6d8a63220de0678596bee707fe2601a72c341f8f2be1b5054809f57b3.

At 1715 the target splits into a 17-position main polygon (SHA-256 9173f390e8cb00c01398edc1ea6ba2647a53d6dbacd364ab62dc721f4dac53f1) and a four-position northwestern fragment (SHA-256 8ed3c680f28e1d76cedf9089a25763ac110a005ce8ae8fe8f8662c36e2a4ebf2).

The main shape consistently includes Kandy, Matale, Dambulla, Nuwara Eliya, Badulla, Mahiyangana, Kurunegala, Anuradhapura and Polonnaruwa, while excluding Ratnapura and Kegalle as well as all audited coastal points; it is a broad inland locator with historical overreach and omissions.
At 1600 the target is absent under a broad saylan feature; at 1815 it disappears into ceylon-1815 and remains absent in 1878. The exact endpoint aligns with annexation even though the start is late.

Daily-life evidence distinguishes eyewitness description, architecture, legal history, manuscripts, museum objects and later continuity. Family forms, schooling, medicine and sanitation are presented with regional and source limits.

The language sample is exact formal Sinhala from Article 5 of the bilingual Kandyan Convention, dated 2 March 1815, with original script, scholarly-style transliteration, translation and explicit warning that it is legal language rather than ordinary speech.
A direct atlas successor to ceylon-1815 is used because the 1815 seam and historical annexation agree; this does not imply cultural disappearance.
